title: LA HB639: Requires disclosure of the use of artificial intelligence in telephone campaign communications

obligations: Provide a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of the call that it was created using artificial intelligence when making or causing to be made any telephone call or automated call covered by this Section that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D))
prohibitions: Make or cause to be made any telephone call or automated call covered by this Section that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure, without providing a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of the call that it was created using artificial intelligence (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D))
reading.what_it_does: Requires a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of any telephone call or automated call in a telephone campaign communication that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure. It defines relevant terms, provides exemptions for certain service providers and broadcasters, sets civil fines, and assigns enforcement to the Board of Ethics.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence: has the same meaning as provided in R.S. 14:73.14 (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(1))
Automated call: includes any call using a prerecorded or artificial voice as part of a calling campaign to deliver information (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(2))
Candidate, person, political committee or committee, principal campaign committee, subsidiary committee, and public office: have the meanings provided in R.S. 18:1483 (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(3))
Elected public official: means an individual who holds public office in this state or any other state in the United States or holds any federal office (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(4))
Limited public figure: means a person who is not a household name but has found themselves in the forefront of a public controversy (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(5))

Message testing: means studying for research purposes how individuals react to positive or negative information on a candidate, elected public official, or ballot proposition (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(6))

Public figure: means a person who is intimately involved in the resolution of important public questions, or by reason of his fame shapes events in areas of concern to society, a famous person, or person of prominence who performs services at discrete events, such as speeches, public appearances, or similar events, for compensation on a per-event basis (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(7))
compliance_steps: Identify whether any telephone campaign communications are created using artificial intelligence and use the voice of a public figure, elected official, or limited public figure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
If so, ensure each such call includes a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning that it was created using artificial intelligence (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
Train personnel and vendors who make or cause calls to include the required disclosure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
Monitor compliance to avoid repeat violations that carry higher fines (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(G)).
Be prepared for enforcement by the Board of Ethics (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(H); Sec. 2, R.S. 42:1132(D)).

notable_exemptions: An interactive computer service as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230 is not liable as a result of content provided by another person (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(F)(1)).

An internet service provider, cloud provider, cybersecurity provider, or any provider of an information service as defined by 47 U.S.C. 153(24) or a telecommunications service as defined by 47 U.S.C. 153(53) is not liable as a result of content provided by another person (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(F)(2)).

What it does

Requires a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of any telephone call or automated call in a telephone campaign communication that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure. It defines relevant terms, provides exemptions for certain service providers and broadcasters, sets civil fines, and assigns enforcement to the Board of Ethics.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who makes or causes to be made a telephone call or automated call covered by R.S. 18:1463.1 that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D))

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: has the same meaning as provided in R.S. 14:73.14 (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(1))
  • Automated call: includes any call using a prerecorded or artificial voice as part of a calling campaign to deliver information (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(2))
  • Candidate, person, political committee or committee, principal campaign committee, subsidiary committee, and public office: have the meanings provided in R.S. 18:1483 (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(3))
  • Elected public official: means an individual who holds public office in this state or any other state in the United States or holds any federal office (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(4))
  • Limited public figure: means a person who is not a household name but has found themselves in the forefront of a public controversy (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(5))
  • Message testing: means studying for research purposes how individuals react to positive or negative information on a candidate, elected public official, or ballot proposition (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(6))
  • Public figure: means a person who is intimately involved in the resolution of important public questions, or by reason of his fame shapes events in areas of concern to society, a famous person, or person of prominence who performs services at discrete events, such as speeches, public appearances, or similar events, for compensation on a per-event basis (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(E)(7))

Obligations

  • Provide a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of the call that it was created using artificial intelligence when making or causing to be made any telephone call or automated call covered by this Section that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D))

Prohibitions

  • Make or cause to be made any telephone call or automated call covered by this Section that is created using artificial intelligence and uses the voice of a public figure, including an elected official or limited public figure, without providing a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of the call that it was created using artificial intelligence (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D))

Penalties and enforcement

The Board of Ethics shall administer and enforce the provisions of R.S. 18:1463.1 (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(H); Sec. 2, R.S. 42:1132(D)). A violation may be punished by a civil fine not to exceed two thousand five hundred dollars; a second or subsequent violation may be punished by a civil fine not to exceed five thousand dollars (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(G)). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organization deploying artificial intelligence in telephone campaign communications that use the voice of a public figure, elected official, or limited public figure must include a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning of each call that it was created using artificial intelligence (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
  • Failure to include the required disclosure can result in a civil fine up to two thousand five hundred dollars for a first violation and up to five thousand dollars for a second or subsequent violation (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(G)).
  • The Board of Ethics has authority to administer and enforce these requirements (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(H); Sec. 2, R.S. 42:1132(D)).
  • Interactive computer services, internet service providers, cloud providers, cybersecurity providers, information service providers, telecommunications service providers, and radio or television broadcasters are not liable for content provided by another person (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(F)(1)-(3)).

Notable exemptions

  • An interactive computer service as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230 is not liable as a result of content provided by another person (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(F)(1)).
  • An internet service provider, cloud provider, cybersecurity provider, or any provider of an information service as defined by 47 U.S.C. 153(24) or a telecommunications service as defined by 47 U.S.C. 153(53) is not liable as a result of content provided by another person (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(F)(2)).
  • A radio or television broadcaster, including a cable or satellite television operator, programmer, or producer, is not liable as a result of content provided by another person (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(F)(3)).

Compliance steps

  • Identify whether any telephone campaign communications are created using artificial intelligence and use the voice of a public figure, elected official, or limited public figure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
  • If so, ensure each such call includes a clear and understandable disclosure at the beginning that it was created using artificial intelligence (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
  • Train personnel and vendors who make or cause calls to include the required disclosure (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(D)).
  • Monitor compliance to avoid repeat violations that carry higher fines (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(G)).
  • Be prepared for enforcement by the Board of Ethics (Sec. 1, R.S. 18:1463.1(H); Sec. 2, R.S. 42:1132(D)).
